The initial configuration consists of a chain of shapes: a pink rectangle (shape 1), a blue rectangle (shape 2) connected by hinge A, a teal triangle (shape 3) connected by hinge B, and a yellow triangle (shape 4) connected by hinge C. All shapes are initially aligned horizontally, pointing to the right.

The target configuration shows a folded shape where:
- The bottom horizontal segment corresponds to shape 1 (fixed in position and orientation).
- The vertical segment on the right corresponds to shape 2, oriented vertically upward.
- The horizontal segment extending left from the top of shape 2 corresponds to shape 3, oriented horizontally to the left.
- The top triangle, pointing upward, corresponds to shape 4.

To achieve this:
- Rotating hinge A by 90° counterclockwise rotates shapes 2, 3, and 4 around A, orienting shape 2 vertically upward (90° direction).
- Rotating hinge B by 90° counterclockwise rotates shapes 3 and 4 around B, changing the direction of shape 3 to horizontal left (180° direction).
- Rotating hinge C by 270° counterclockwise rotates shape 4 around C. Since shape 3 is at 180° direction, adding 270° (which is equivalent to -90°) results in a 90° direction for shape 4, orienting it upward to match the target.

The sequence of rotations (A 90°, B 90°, C 270°) transforms the initial configuration to the target. Rotations are multiples of 90° and applied counterclockwise as required.

- Rotating hinge C by 90° anti-clockwise folds the blue triangle (shape 3) downward to its final orientation in the target, as the pink triangle is at 180° absolute orientation.

This sequence achieves the target configuration:
- Shape 0 (diamond) remains at 0°.
- Shape 1 (yellow) has an absolute orientation of 270°.
- Shape 2 (pink) has an absolute orientation of 270° + 270° = 540° ≡ 180°.
- Shape 3 (blue) has an absolute orientation of 180° + 90° = 270°.

The rotations are valid as they are multiples of 90° and maintain the connections throughout.
